bug_description.original:
Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=4542532443045888

Project: kimageformats
Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer
Fuzz Target: kimgio_heif_fuzzer
Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_kimageformats
Platform Id: linux

Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 3
Crash Address: 0x6080000002a0
Crash State:
  HEIFHandler::ensureDecoder
  HEIFHandler::read
  kimgio_fuzzer.cc
  
Sanitizer: address
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged `poc` is 28 bytes: four spaces, `ftypheic`, then 16 spaces (`20 20 20 20 66 74 79 70 68 65 69 63 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`). `HEIFHandler::ensureDecoder()` reads those bytes into `buffer`; `HEIFHandler::isSupportedBMFFType()` admits them because the 28-byte header contains `ftyp` at offset 4 and major brand `heic` at offset 8. `heif_context_read_from_memory()` then rejects the malformed, header-only payload and returns `struct heif_error err`. In libheif, `heif_context_read_from_memory()` returns `err.error_struct(ctx->context.get())`, and `Error::error_struct()` stores `err.message = error_buffer->get_error()`, so `err.message` aliases the `HeifContext`'s inherited `ErrorBuffer` string instead of a copied buffer. Vulnerable `ensureDecoder()` takes the `if (err.code)` branch, executes `heif_context_free(ctx)` first, and only then logs `err.message` with `qWarning()`. Because `heif_context_free()` deletes the wrapper holding the last `shared_ptr<HeifContext>`, the `ErrorBuffer` backing `err.message` is freed before the log call. Qt's logging path converts that dangling `const char *` through `operator<<` -> `QString::fromUtf8` -> `strlen`, and Stage 01's saved run reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 3` at `kimageformats/src/imageformats/heif.cpp:437`. The patch fixes this exact lifetime error by moving each `qWarning() << err.message` before the corresponding `heif_context_free(ctx)` and handle-release sequence.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled QIODevice bytes and materializes them into the QByteArray used by the BMFF probe and the later libheif parse call.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` is exactly 28 bytes: `20 20 20 20 66 74 79 70 68 65 69 63 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`. This line copies those bytes from the fuzz harness's QBuffer into `buffer`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Project-level sink. The error logger consumes `err.message` after its backing storage was freed, and Qt's `QDebug` path reaches the saved `strlen` read.
sink.note: Stage 01's ASan trace is `__interceptor_strlen -> fromUtf8 -> operator<< -> HEIFHandler::ensureDecoder` at this exact statement.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the `err.code` error path, vulnerable code frees `ctx` before the last use of `err.message`, even though libheif made `err.message` point into `ctx->context`'s `ErrorBuffer`.
root_cause.note: The fix hunk moves the `qWarning() << err.message` calls above `heif_context_free(ctx)` in this branch and the analogous `heif_context_get_primary_image_handle` and `heif_decode_image` error branches.

parser_admitted.description: The saved 28-byte witness is exactly long enough for the BMFF probe and contains `ftypheic` at offsets 4..11, so `isSupportedBMFFType()` returns true and `ensureDecoder()` reaches the failing libheif parse path.

tainted_value_origin.description: Libheif materializes the later-dangling pointer here by making `heif_error.message` alias the `HeifContext`'s inherited `ErrorBuffer`. `HEIFHandler::ensureDecoder` then carries this pointer across `heif_context_free(ctx)`.

fine_trace.note: The format gate admits this witness because `header.size() == 28`, bytes 4..7 are `ftyp`, and bytes 8..11 are `heic`, so `ensureDecoder()` does not return early at the unsupported-type check.

Allocates the libheif wrapper object later invalidated on the error path. `heif_context_alloc()` initializes `ctx->context = std::make_shared<HeifContext>()`, so this `ctx` owns the `HeifContext` and its inherited `ErrorBuffer`.

fine_trace.code: struct heif_error err = heif_context_read_from_memory(ctx, static_cast<const void *>(buffer.constData()), buffer.size(), nullptr);
fine_trace.note: The admitted 28-byte header stub is handed to libheif. On the saved witness this parse call fails, so `err.code` becomes nonzero and the returned `heif_error` is prepared for the error-handling path.

Libheif materializes the pointer later used by kimageformats. `heif_context_read_from_memory()` returns `err.error_struct(ctx->context.get())`, `HeifContext` inherits `ErrorBuffer`, and `ErrorBuffer::set_error()` stores the formatted message in an internal `std::string`, so `err.message` aliases `ctx->context` storage instead of an independent copy.
Because libheif rejected the malformed payload, the error branch is taken and the function proceeds into the free-then-log sequence.

Root cause. `heif_context_free()` is a thin `delete ctx;`, and `heif_context`'s only field is the `shared_ptr<HeifContext>` from step 3. That delete releases the `ErrorBuffer` string backing `err.message`, so the pointer established in step 5 becomes dangling before its last use.

Sink. Qt converts `err.message` through `QDebug` and `QString::fromUtf8`, which immediately sizes the dangling C string with `strlen`. Stage 01's saved ASan report is `heap-use-after-free READ of size 3` with stack `__interceptor_strlen -> fromUtf8 -> operator<< -> HEIFHandler::ensureDecoder`.

free_context.description: Closest project-level free site. The saved ASan free stack then descends through `heif_context_free` -> `delete ctx` -> `HeifContext::~HeifContext` / `~ErrorBuffer`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The saved allocation stack resolves only into libc++ string storage, but the source-level free-before-use at `heif.cpp:436-437` matches the saved free stack and the patch hunk exactly.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `__interceptor_strlen -> fromUtf8 -> operator<< -> HEIFHandler::ensureDecoder -> HEIFHandler::read -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, and the fine trace refines the same project path with the in-function HEIF brand gate, libheif error-message aliasing, and the free-before-log lifetime break at `heif.cpp:436-437`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_54246 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged 28-byte file to `/out/kimgio_heif_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 3` with stack `__interceptor_strlen -> fromUtf8 -> operator<< -> HEIFHandler::ensureDecoder`.

format.name: HEIF/BMFF header stub
format.contract: This exact staged `poc` is the 28-byte buffer `20 20 20 20 66 74 79 70 68 65 69 63 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`. The only verified trigger facts are that `HEIFHandler::isSupportedBMFFType()` accepts it as `ftyp` / `heic`, `heif_context_read_from_memory()` returns an error on the malformed header-only payload, and vulnerable `HEIFHandler::ensureDecoder()` logs `err.message` after `heif_context_free(ctx)`, reproducing the saved heap-use-after-free read.
